text: The demand to the guarantors and co-borrowers is dispatched as the workflow kit's Notify activity on task queue rwb-comms in namespace rwb-recovery, one call per addressee, with the GuarantorNotice payload typed by RWB-S3-E4017-CON; rwb-guarantee publishes no event for it, consumes no REST operation to reach rwb-comms, and sends no name, no address and no customer identifier, because rwb-comms resolves the addressee and issues the letter on its own path.
why: FSD S3 A2.5.2 names only 'WIN, Workbench' as integration points with no contract, Architecture v5 slide 13 draws T and E from S3 to P6 and no R while the note says route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal and never REST, and the Ownership Map gives S3 zero published events, so neither a service event nor a REST contract of this service can carry the demand.
read: Architecture v5 slide 13 (S3 Guarantee row and P6 Comms row) and slide 8 (VIN letter file INT-14, rwb-comms on the ACE notification path); Temporal and Drools Design slide 12 (L3 workflow kit with Notify, L4 activity contracts on rwb-<svc>); Context pack S3 (ownership rows: events 0, two claim operations, workflow GuaranteeClaimWorkflow); FSD S3 v3 A2.5.2 and A2.5.3.1 BR-S3-005; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and R7.2 s17
applied_in: RWB-S3-E4017-APP sections 1, 4 steps 6 to 9, 5 X5 and X6, 7 Target reading, 8 BR4 and BR10 to BR12, 12.3, 12.5 and 12.8; RWB-S3-E4017-CON sections 7 (AC2 and AC3), 8 (BR2 to BR4, BR8), 12.3 and 12.5
confirm: P6 owner of the letter with the rwb-guarantee tech lead at the wave 3 contract freeze
impact: If rwb-comms cannot take the demand as an activity on its queue, one REST operation or one event of rwb-comms appears as a consumed contract and a C dependency is added to the notice story; the payload and the criteria do not change.

text: The case, the party and the case status stay rwb-case's. The addressees are the parties of the case signal whose role is a guarantor or a co-borrower, the case status arrives on the same signal, rwb-guarantee reports the stage outcome of R-GUA-06 to the parent CaseWorkflow and reads no recovery_case, case_party or timer row.
why: The legacy story's data section names recovery_case, case_party and timer, the acceptance criterion that names a case state ends with a status move, Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the case, its state, its queues and its timers to rwb-case, DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables, and the Work Package lists no contract dependency that a case REST call would need.
read: Architecture v5 slide 41 (rwb-case owns the case, its state, queues, tasks and timers) and slide 13 (S3 rwb-guarantee); Temporal and Drools Design slides 13 and 14 (CaseWorkflow is the parent and each stage a child, the case router forwards events as signals); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01; Context pack S3 ownership rows
applied_in: RWB-S3-E4017-APP sections 1, 4 steps 2, 5 and 8, 7 Target reading, 9 State transitions, 11 Data and 12.7; RWB-S3-E4017-CON sections 7 (AC5), 8 (BR12), 11 and 12.8
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-guarantee with the P3 owner of the case workflow at the wave 3 build start
impact: If the parent does not own the status move or the parties, a stage would have to call rwb-case over REST and a C dependency would appear on the plan; no business rule changes either way.

text: The notice period by product and the notice due date are values in force, and the notice clock is a durable Temporal timer inside GuaranteeClaimWorkflow rather than a timer row or a Schedule: the routing workbook gives the period only as 'Notice period by product' in its service-level column, this run exports it as a parameter key, and the due date is the notice-period start plus that period, recorded with the notice on the local decision record because no guarantee_claim column holds it.
why: R-GUA-06 gives the notice its own clock and the legacy data table names timer because the monolith parked the wait in a row, no parameter key or field identifier exists for the period or the due date, Architecture v5 slide 42 retires the TimerDue event because the clock lives inside the workflow, and TSD S3 T3.1 gives guarantee_claim no notice date.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-GUA-06 ('Notice period by product'); TSD S3 v2 T4 (GUARANTEE, 17 states) and T3.1 (DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022); Temporal and Drools Design slides 12, 13 and 18; Architecture v5 slide 42 event 18; FSD S3 v3 A2.5.3.1 BR-S3-005
applied_in: RWB-S3-E4017-APP sections 3, 4 steps 3, 7 and 10, 7 Target reading, 8 BR5, BR6 and BR8, 12.5, 12.6 and 13; RWB-S3-E4017-CON sections 7 (AC4), 8 (BR5, BR6, BR11) and 12.6
confirm: P3 owner of the parameters with the rwb-guarantee tech lead at the wave 3 build start
impact: If the parameter set cannot carry the period, it becomes a reference-data row of the GUARANTEE package; the criteria hold either way, because none of them names a number of days.

text: The notice rides the claim update operation that RWB-S3-E4013-CON publishes as PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} on base /api/recovery/guarantee/v1 and declares no path of its own; its payload is GuarantorNotice with seven properties and five required, of which claimId, caseId and the claim deadline map to guarantee_claim fields and partyRef, partyRole, noticeType, templateCode and noticeDueDate are a reference or a computed value with no column.
why: The legacy story's endpoint table lists the claim create and the claim update only, TSD S3 T-A.1 API-S3-001 and API-S3-002 name the same two, no source publishes a notice body or a notice path, and TSD S3 T3.1 gives the table no notice field, so the payload can only ride an existing operation and its unmapped properties must be stated as such.
read: TSD S3 v2 T-A.1 (API-S3-001, API-S3-002) and T-A.2 and T3.1; legacy RWB-E4-017 section 19 (endpoint table) and section 11 (data table); Architecture v5 slide 13 (S3 owns two claim operations); Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence and R5.5 DP-13
applied_in: RWB-S3-E4017-CON sections 3, 7 (AC1 and AC4), 11, 12.1 and 13; RWB-S3-E4017-APP sections 3, 12.1 and 12.7
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-guarantee tech lead at the wave 3 contract freeze
impact: If a separate notice path is published, one more operation and one more client binding appear in the service document; the template rule, the delivery path and the criteria do not change.
